text: October twenty fifteen. Satellites detect more than eighty thousand fires across Sumatra and Kalimantan.
Haze covers Singapore. In one region, hourly P M two point five reaches four hundred and seventy-one micrograms.
Can wind, rainfall and regional fires help us understand, and predict, these haze episodes?
Our 2015 study tested this. Adding wind and rain made six-hour predictions worse. Adding fires made them worse again.
So how should an AI science team decide what evidence to trust, and when to abstain? Training a model takes minutes. Knowing whether to trust it takes evidence.
Empi-raxis is an AI science team that has to earn its conclusions.
A person asks: can Singapore's P M two point five be predicted six hours ahead, and does a neural network justify its cost?
One local model, Meta's Muse Glimmer, plays four roles. Each role can only propose. Code checks every proposal, and twice it refused one.
The lead expected a statistical model to win, and still asked for a neural challenger.
Trusted code tuned a ridge on three rolling yearly folds. The strongest penalty, ten thousand, gave the lowest error.
Then it trained a compact temporal network. Validation loss was best at epoch five, so training stopped at epoch eight.
The saved network was reloaded, and reproduced all forty-three thousand predictions exactly.
An independent evaluator scored every model on the same rows. The neural network did not beat the ridge.
And in high pollution hours, every learned model lost to simply repeating the last value.
So the lead recommended keeping the existing lagged ridge. These years were used before, so this is not an independent test.
No model approves its own work. The decision waits for a person, with a signed key.
When Muse asked for fresh official data, the owner signed the request. Seventeen of three hundred and fifty values disagree with the archive, and stay visible.
Sometimes, the right answer is no. Reject a reused model. Abstain on a fire source. Ask a person for better imagery.
Every step is hash-chained, and replays without a model. Five real predictions, made hours ahead, were scored against what Singapore later published.
Next, we will test whether wind, rain, fire, satellite and soil-moisture data add real skill. That study is planned. It has no results yet.
Empi-raxis. Not more autonomy. Better evidence.
